title: Hence no grace is sufficient without being efficacious
source_text: IV. Unde sequitur omnibus qui actu non convertuntur & bene operantur, deesse aliquod divinum auxilium ad agendum necessarium atque praerequisitum; adeoque illos non debere dici gratiam sufficientem habere ut sese convertant & bene operentur: cum illud solum dici debeat sufficiens, quod necessaria omnia complectitur. Quicunque autem auxilia omnia ad bonum aliquod opus praevia & necessaria habet, illum infallibiliter & certo bene acturum: & sic omnem gratiam, quae vere dici possit sufficiens, etiam efficacem esse: ac proinde frustra gratiam salutarem Christi Redemptoris, quae lapso homini necessaria est, in Scholis solere distingui in efficacem & sufficientem.
pass_a_gloss: IV. Whence it follows that to all who do not actually turn and work well, some divine help is lacking, necessary for acting and prerequired; and so that they ought not to be said to have sufficient grace to turn themselves and work well: since that alone ought to be called sufficient, which embraces all necessary things. But whoever has all the helps prior and necessary for some good work, he will infallibly and certainly act well: and thus every grace, which can truly be called sufficient, is also efficacious: and therefore in vain is the saving grace of Christ the Redeemer, which is necessary to fallen man, wont in the Schools to be distinguished into efficacious and sufficient.
pass_b_english: Thesis IV. It follows that everyone who does not actually turn and do good lacks some divine aid that action requires and presupposes. Such people, then, should not be said to have sufficient grace for turning and doing good, since only what includes everything needed deserves the name sufficient.

Whoever has every aid that a good work requires beforehand will infallibly and surely perform it. So every grace that can truly be called sufficient is efficacious as well, and the Schools' custom of dividing the saving grace of Christ the Redeemer, which fallen humanity needs, into efficacious and sufficient is pointless.

lemmas.gloss: will infallibly and certainly act well

choices.why: The standard scholastic pair of the de auxiliis controversy; kept constant across the locus.

bible_refs: Cornelius Jansenius, Augustinus (Louvain, 1640), tome 3, De gratia Christi Salvatoris.
